title: KCET 2020 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: The percentage of s-character in the hybrid orbitals of nitrogen in NO$_2^+$, NO$_3^-$ and NH$_4^+$ respectively are:
questions.explanation: NO$_2^+$ is linear (sp, 50% s), NO$_3^-$ is trigonal planar (sp$^2$, 33.3% s) and NH$_4^+$ is tetrahedral (sp$^3$, 25% s).

questions.q: The formal charge on the central oxygen atom in ozone is
questions.explanation: In the resonance structure of O$_3$, the central O has 3 bonds (one double, one single, counted as 3 sigma+pi bonding pairs shared) and one lone pair: formal charge = 6 - 2 - 3 = +1.

questions.q: When the same quantity of heat is absorbed by a system at two different temperatures T$_1$ and T$_2$, such that T$_1$ > T$_2$, the changes in entropies are $\Delta S_1$ and $\Delta S_2$ respectively. Then:
questions.explanation: $\Delta S = q/T$ for the same q; since T$_1$ > T$_2$, dividing by the larger temperature gives the smaller entropy change, so $\Delta S_1 < \Delta S_2$.

questions.q: The oxidation number of nitrogen atoms in NH$_4$NO$_3$ are
questions.explanation: In NH$_4^+$, N is -3 (each H is +1, ion charge +1); in NO$_3^-$, N is +5 (each O is -2, ion charge -1).

questions.q: A Lewis acid 'X' reacts with LiAlH$_4$ in ether medium to give a highly toxic gas. This gas when heated with NH$_3$ gives a compound commonly known as inorganic benzene. The gas is
questions.explanation: BF$_3$ (X) reacts with LiAlH$_4$ to give diborane B$_2$H$_6$, which on heating with NH$_3$ forms borazine (B$_3$N$_3$H$_6$), the 'inorganic benzene'.

questions.q: The oxide of potassium that does not exist is
questions.explanation: Potassium forms the normal oxide K$_2$O, the peroxide K$_2$O$_2$ and the superoxide KO$_2$, but a sesquioxide-type K$_2$O$_3$ is not known.

questions.q: The metal that produces H$_2$ with both dil. HCl and NaOH(aq) is
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles of Metallurgy
questions.explanation: Zinc is amphoteric and liberates H$_2$ gas with both dilute acids and dilute alkalis; Fe, Mg and Ca do not react with NaOH(aq).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a pair of functional isomers?
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: C$_2$H$_5$OC$_2$H$_5$ and C$_3$H$_7$OCH$_3$ are both ethers (same functional group), so they are chain isomers, not functional isomers; the other pairs each contain two different functional groups with the same molecular formula.

questions.q: Identify 'X' in the following reaction: benzene + 6Cl$_2$ (excess) $\xrightarrow[\text{dark, cold}]{\text{Anhydrous AlCl}_3}$ X + 6HCl
options: Hexachlorobenzene (all six ring H replaced by Cl)
questions.explanation: Release of 6 mol HCl means all six ring hydrogens undergo electrophilic substitution by Cl$_2$/AlCl$_3$, giving hexachlorobenzene (aromatic ring retained).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a green house gas?
questions.explanation: O$_2$ is not a greenhouse gas; KEA's key also accepted NO$_2$ (not one of the standard greenhouse gases CO$_2$, CH$_4$, N$_2$O, CFCs, O$_3$, water vapour) as correct.

questions.q: A metal exists as an oxide with formula M$_{0.96}$O. Metal M can exist as M$^{+2}$ and M$^{+3}$ in its oxide M$_{0.96}$O. The percentage of M$^{+3}$ in the oxide is, nearly
questions.explanation: Charge balance: 2(0.96-x) + 3x = 2 gives x = 0.08 mol M$^{3+}$ per 0.96 mol metal, i.e. 0.08/0.96 = 8.3%.

questions.q: A metal crystallises in face centred cubic structure with metallic radius $\sqrt2$ A°. The volume of the unit cell (in m$^3$) is
questions.explanation: For fcc, edge $a = 2\sqrt2\,r = 2\sqrt2\times\sqrt2 = 4$ A° $= 4\times10^{-10}$ m; volume $= a^3 = 6.4\times10^{-29}$ m$^3$.

questions.q: Silicon doped with gallium forms
options: both n and p type semiconductor
questions.explanation: Gallium (group 13) has one less valence electron than Si, creating electron-deficient holes, giving a p-type semiconductor.

questions.q: The pair of electrolytes that possess the same value for the constant (A) in the Debye-Huckel-Onsagar equation, $\lambda_m = \lambda_m^\circ - A\sqrt C$ is
questions.explanation: The constant A depends only on the charge type (valence factor) of the electrolyte; NH$_4$Cl and NaBr are both 1:1 electrolytes and so share the same A, unlike the other mixed-valence pairs.

questions.q: Which of the following pair of solutions is isotonic?
questions.explanation: Isotonic solutions need equal total particle concentration (i$\times$C): 0.01 M BaCl$_2$ (i=3) gives 0.03 M, and 0.015 M NaCl (i=2) also gives 0.03 M.

questions.q: Solute 'X' dimerises in water to the extent of 80%. 2.5g of 'X' in 100g of water increases the boiling point by 0.3°C. [K$_b$ = 0.52 K kg mol$^{-1}$] 'X' is molar mass is
questions.explanation: Van't Hoff factor $i = 1-\alpha+\alpha/2 = 1-0.8+0.4 = 0.6$. $\Delta T_b = iK_b\dfrac{w\times1000}{M\times W}$ gives $0.3 = 0.6\times0.52\times\dfrac{2.5\times1000}{M\times100}$, so $M = 26$.

questions.q: Given: E$^\circ_{Fe^{+3}/Fe^{+2}}$ = +0.76 V and E$^\circ_{I_2/I^-}$ = +0.55 V. The equilibrium constant for the reaction taking place in the galvanic cell consisting of the above two electrodes is $\left[\dfrac{2.303RT}{F}=0.06\right]$
If an aqueous solution of NaF is electrolyzed between inert electrodes, the product obtained at anode is
questions.explanation: F$^-$ is very difficult to oxidise (very high oxidation potential required), so water is preferentially oxidised at the anode to give O$_2$.

questions.q: In which of the following cases a chemical reaction is possible?
options: gold ornaments are washed with dil HCl
ZnSO$_{4(aq)}$ is placed in a copper vessel
AgNO$_3$ solution is stirred with a copper spoon
Conc. HNO$_3$ is stored in a platinum vessel
questions.explanation: Copper, being more reactive than silver, displaces Ag from AgNO$_3$ solution: Cu + 2AgNO$_3\to$Cu(NO$_3$)$_2$ + 2Ag; gold, platinum and copper-in-ZnSO$_4$ show no reaction.

questions.q: The time required for 60% completion of a first order reaction is 50 min. The time required for 93.6% completion of the same reaction will be
questions.explanation: $t\propto\log\dfrac{100}{100-x}$; ratio of times = $\log(100/6.4)/\log(100/40) = \log15.625/\log2.5 = 3$, so t$_2$ = 3$\times$50 = 150 min.

questions.q: For an elementary reaction 2A + 3B $\to$ 4C + D the rate of appearance of C at time 't' is 2.8 $\times$ 10$^{-3}$ mol L$^{-1}$S$^{-1}$. Rate of disappearance of B at 't' will be
questions.explanation: Rate $= \dfrac14\dfrac{d[C]}{dt} = \dfrac13\left(-\dfrac{d[B]}{dt}\right)$, so $-\dfrac{d[B]}{dt} = \dfrac34\times\dfrac{d[C]}{dt} = \dfrac34(2.8\times10^{-3})$.

questions.q: The rate constant of a reaction is given by k = PZe$^{-Ea/RT}$ under standard notation. In order to speed up the reaction, which of the following factors has to be decreased?
questions.explanation: Rate constant increases as the activation energy E$_a$ decreases (it appears with a negative sign in the exponent).

questions.q: A sol of AgI is prepared by mixing equal volumes of 0.1 M AgNO$_3$ and 0.2 M KI, which of the following statement is correct?
options: Sol obtained is a negative sol with I$^-$ adsorbed on AgI.
Sol obtained is a negative sol with NO$_3^-$ adsorbed on AgI.
Sol obtained is a positive sol with Ag$^+$ adsorbed on AgI.
Sol obtained is a positive sol with K$^+$ adsorbed on AgI.
questions.explanation: KI is in stoichiometric excess (0.2 M vs 0.1 M AgNO$_3$ in equal volumes), so excess I$^-$ is preferentially adsorbed, giving a negative sol.

questions.q: During Adsorption of a gas on a solid
questions.explanation: Adsorption is spontaneous ($\Delta G<0$), exothermic ($\Delta H<0$), and randomness decreases as gas molecules get ordered on the surface ($\Delta S<0$).

questions.q: Copper is extracted from copper pyrites by
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles of Metallurgy
questions.explanation: After roasting, Cu$_2$S and Cu$_2$O formed react with each other in the self/auto-reduction step: 2Cu$_2$O + Cu$_2$S $\to$ 6Cu + SO$_2$.

questions.q: Function of potassium ethylxanthate in froth floatation process is to make the ore
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles of Metallurgy
questions.explanation: Potassium ethylxanthate is a collector that coats the sulphide ore particles, making them hydrophobic so they attach to air bubbles and rise in the froth.

questions.q: Sulphide ore on roasting gives a gas X. X reacts with Cl$_2$ in the presence of activated charcoal to give Y. Y is:
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles of Metallurgy
questions.explanation: Roasting a sulphide ore gives SO$_2$ (X); SO$_2$ + Cl$_2$ over charcoal catalyst gives sulfuryl chloride, SO$_2$Cl$_2$ (Y).

questions.q: Aqueous solution of a salt (A) forms a dense white precipitate with BaCl$_2$ solution. The precipitate dissolves in dilute HCl to produce a gas (B) which decolourises acidified KMnO$_4$ solution. A and B respectively are:
questions.explanation: BaSO$_3$ is a white precipitate that (unlike BaSO$_4$) dissolves in dilute HCl releasing SO$_2$ gas, which decolourises acidified KMnO$_4$; KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: Bond angle in PH$_4^+$ is more than that of PH$_3$. This is because
options: hybridisation of P changes when PH$_3$ is converted to PH$_4^+$
lonepair-bond pair repulsion exists in PH$_3$
questions.explanation: PH$_3$ has a lone pair on P causing extra lone pair-bond pair repulsion that compresses the H-P-H angle; PH$_4^+$ has no lone pair, so its tetrahedral angle is larger.

questions.q: Incorrectly matched pair is:
questions.explanation: XeF$_4$ is square planar (sp$^3$d$^2$ with 2 lone pairs), not tetrahedral, so this pairing is incorrect; the other three are correctly matched.

questions.q: Phosphorus pentachloride
options: exists as an ionic solid in which cation has octahedral structure and anion has tetrahedral structure.
on hydrolysis gives an oxo acid of phosphorus which is tribasic.
on hydrolysis gives an oxo acid of phosphorus which is a good reducing agent.
has all the five equivalent bonds.
questions.explanation: PCl$_5$ + 4H$_2$O $\to$ H$_3$PO$_4$ + 5HCl; orthophosphoric acid H$_3$PO$_4$ is tribasic (three ionisable OH groups).

questions.q: Identify the set of paramagnetic ions among the following:
questions.explanation: Ti$^{3+}$(d$^1$), Cu$^{2+}$(d$^9$) and Mn$^{3+}$(d$^4$) all have unpaired electrons (paramagnetic); the other sets each contain a d$^0$ or d$^{10}$ (diamagnetic) ion (Sc$^{3+}$, Ti$^{4+}$, Zn$^{2+}$).

questions.q: How many moles of acidified K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ is required to liberate 6 moles of I$_2$ from an aqueous solution of I$^-$?
questions.explanation: Cr$_2$O$_7^{2-}$ + 6I$^-$ + 14H$^+ \to$ 2Cr$^{3+}$ + 3I$_2$ + 7H$_2$O; 1 mol dichromate liberates 3 mol I$_2$, so 6 mol I$_2$ needs 2 mol K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$.

questions.q: Cu$_2$Cl$_2$ and CuCl$_2$ in aqueous medium
options: Cu$_2$Cl$_2$ is more stable than CuCl$_2$
CuCl$_2$ is more stable than Cu$_2$Cl$_2$
Stability of Cu$_2$Cl$_2$ is equal to stability of CuCl$_2$
questions.explanation: In water, the higher hydration enthalpy of Cu$^{2+}$ more than compensates for its higher ionisation energy compared to Cu$^+$, so Cu$^{2+}$ (CuCl$_2$) is more stable in aqueous medium; Cu$^+$ disproportionates.

questions.q: The co-ordination number of Fe and Co in the complex ions, [Fe(C$_2$O$_4$)$_3$]$^{3-}$ and [Co(SCN)$_4$]$^{2-}$ are respectively:
questions.explanation: Oxalate is a bidentate ligand, so 3 oxalates give coordination number 6 for Fe; SCN$^-$ is monodentate, so 4 SCN$^-$ give coordination number 4 for Co.

questions.q: Number of stereoisomers exhibited by [Co(en)$_2$Cl$_2$]$^+$ is
questions.explanation: This [M(AA)$_2$B$_2$] complex shows a chiral cis form (a pair of enantiomers) and an achiral trans form, giving 3 stereoisomers in total.

questions.q: Give the IUPAC name of [Pt(NH$_3$)$_4$][PtCl$_4$] is
options: tetra ammine platinum(II) tetra chlorido platinate(II)
tetra ammine platinum(o) tetra chlorido platinum(IV)
tetra ammine platinate(II) tetra chlorido platinum(II)
tetra ammine platinate(o) tetra chlorido platinum(IV)
questions.explanation: The cation [Pt(NH$_3$)$_4$]$^{2+}$ is tetraamminplatinum(II) and the anion [PtCl$_4$]$^{2-}$ is tetrachloridoplatinate(II).

questions.q: Prolonged exposure of chloroform in humans may cause damage to liver. It is due to the formation of the following compound:
questions.explanation: Chloroform is slowly oxidised by air/light to the highly toxic gas phosgene (COCl$_2$), which damages the liver.

questions.q: Which of the following halide shows highest reactivity towards S$_N$1 reaction?
questions.explanation: Benzyl chloride ionises readily because the resulting benzylic carbocation is stabilised by resonance with the ring, giving the fastest S$_N$1 reaction; aryl halides resist S$_N$1 altogether.

questions.q: In the reaction: [a branched secondary alkyl magnesium bromide]-MgBr + CH$_3$NH$_2$ $\xrightarrow{\text{Dry ether}}$ X. The number of possible isomers for the organic compound X is
questions.explanation: The acidic N-H of methylamine protonates the Grignard reagent at its chiral carbon; since the carbanion-like carbon can be attacked from either face, the resulting alkane X is obtained as a mixture of 2 stereoisomers (as per KEA key).

questions.q: Which of the following on heating gives an ether as major product? P: C$_6$H$_5$CH$_2$Br + CH$_3$ONa; Q: C$_6$H$_5$ONa + CH$_3$Br; R: (CH$_3$)$_3$C-Cl + CH$_3$ONa; S: C$_6$H$_5$CH=CHCl + CH$_3$ONa
questions.explanation: P and Q both undergo Williamson ether synthesis (S$_N$2 at an unhindered primary/methyl carbon) to give ethers; R (3° halide) undergoes elimination and S (vinylic halide) resists substitution.

questions.q: The steps involved in the conversion of propan-2-ol to propan-1-ol are in the order
options: dehydration, addition of HBr in presence of peroxide, heating with alc. KOH
dehydration, addition of HBr, heating with aq. KOH
heating with PCl$_5$, heating with alc. KOH, acid catalysed addition of water
heating with PCl$_5$, heating with alc. KOH, hydroboration-oxidation
questions.explanation: PCl$_5$ converts propan-2-ol to 2-chloropropane; alc. KOH eliminates it to propene; hydroboration-oxidation adds water anti-Markovnikov to give propan-1-ol.

questions.q: Which of the following is the strongest base?
questions.explanation: Methanol is a weaker acid than water and acetic acid due to the +I effect of the methyl group, so its conjugate base CH$_3$O$^-$ is the strongest base of the four.

questions.q: Benzaldehyde + CH$_3$CHO $\xrightarrow[(2)\ \Delta]{(1)\ \text{dil. NaOH}}$ P. The product 'P' is
options: C$_6$H$_5$-CH$_2$CHO (with an extra CHO on ring)
C$_6$H$_5$-CHO with a CH$_2$CHO substituent on ring
questions.explanation: Benzaldehyde has no alpha-H, so acetaldehyde's alpha carbon attacks it in a cross aldol condensation; dehydration on heating gives cinnamaldehyde, C$_6$H$_5$-CH=CH-CHO.

questions.q: Which of the following has the lowest boiling point?
questions.explanation: Dimethyl ether cannot hydrogen-bond with itself (no O-H/N-H), so it has by far the lowest boiling point compared to the H-bonded formic acid, ethanol and ethylamine.

questions.q: The carbonyl compound that does not undergo aldol condensation is
questions.explanation: Trichloroacetaldehyde (Cl$_3$C-CHO) has no alpha-hydrogen atom, which is essential for aldol condensation.

questions.q: Nitrobenzene $\xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2/\text{FeBr}_3}$ P $\xrightarrow{\text{Sn/conc.HCl}}$ Q $\xrightarrow[\text{dil.HCl}]{\text{(i) NaNO}_2, 273K}$ ... $\xrightarrow{\text{(ii) water, warm}}$ R. The final product R is
options: 3-bromophenol (Br and OH meta to each other)
questions.explanation: NO$_2$ directs Br meta (P = m-bromonitrobenzene); Sn/HCl reduces NO$_2$ to NH$_2$ (Q = m-bromoaniline); diazotisation followed by hydrolysis with warm water replaces N$_2^+$ with OH, giving m-bromophenol.

questions.q: Hinsberg's reagent is
questions.explanation: Hinsberg's reagent, used to distinguish 1°, 2° and 3° amines, is benzenesulfonyl chloride, C$_6$H$_5$SO$_2$Cl.

questions.q: Which one of the following vitamins is not stored in adipose tissue?
questions.explanation: Vitamin B$_6$ is water-soluble and is not stored in fatty (adipose) tissue, unlike the fat-soluble vitamins A, D and E.

questions.q: Hypothyroidism is caused by the deficiency of
questions.explanation: Hypothyroidism results from insufficient secretion of the thyroid hormone thyroxine.

questions.q: C$_1$-C$_4$ glycosidic bond is NOT found in
questions.explanation: Sucrose has a C$_1$-C$_2$ glycosidic linkage (between glucose C1 and fructose C2); starch, maltose and lactose all have C$_1$-C$_4$ linkages.

questions.q: Which of the following polymer has strongest intermolecular forces of attraction?
questions.explanation: Terylene is a polyester fibre; fibres have the strongest intermolecular forces (H-bonding/dipole interactions) among polymer classes, higher than thermoplastics and elastomers.

questions.q: Which of the following monomers can undergo condensation polymerization?
questions.explanation: Glycine, an amino acid with both -NH$_2$ and -COOH groups, undergoes condensation polymerisation to form a polypeptide; the others are alkenes that undergo addition polymerisation.

questions.q: A food additive that acts as an anti-oxidant is
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.explanation: BHA (butylated hydroxyanisole) is added to fats/oils to prevent oxidative rancidity, acting as an antioxidant.

questions.q: Which of the following is not related to drug-enzyme interaction?
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: Chemistry in Everyday Life
questions.explanation: Enzyme inhibitors, competitive inhibition and allosteric (non-active) sites all describe how drugs interact with enzymes; co-enzymes are natural enzyme cofactors, unrelated to a drug's mechanism of action.

questions.q: 0.4 g of dihydrogen is made to react with 7.1 g of dichlorine to form hydrogen chloride. The volume of hydrogen chloride formed at 273 K and 1 bar pressure is
questions.explanation: Moles: H$_2$ = 0.2, Cl$_2$ = 7.1/71 = 0.1 (limiting). H$_2$+Cl$_2\to$2HCl gives 0.2 mol HCl; at 273K, 1 bar molar volume is 22.7 L, so V = 0.2$\times$22.7 = 4.54 L.

questions.q: With regard to photoelectric effect, identify the CORRECT statement among the following:
options: Number of e$^-$ ejected increases with the increase in the intensity of incident light.
Energy of e$^-$ ejected increases with the increase in the intensity of incident light.
Number of e$^-$ ejected increases with the increase in the frequency of incident light.
Number of e$^-$ ejected increases with the increase in work function.
questions.explanation: In the photoelectric effect, the number of photoelectrons ejected depends on the intensity of light, while their kinetic energy depends on the frequency, not the intensity.

questions.q: The last element of the p-block in 6$^{th}$ period is represented by the outer most electronic configuration:
questions.explanation: The last p-block element of period 6 is radon (Z=86), whose configuration is [Xe]4f$^{14}$5d$^{10}$6s$^2$6p$^6$.

questions.q: The conjugate base of NH$_3$ is
questions.explanation: Removing a proton (H$^+$) from NH$_3$ gives the amide ion NH$_2^-$, its conjugate base.

questions.q: A gas mixture contains 25% He and 75% CH$_4$ by volume at a given temperature and pressure. The percentage by mass of methane in the mixture is approximately
questions.explanation: For 100 mol mixture: 25 mol He = 100 g, 75 mol CH$_4$ = 1200 g; mass % CH$_4$ = 1200/1300 $\approx$ 92%.
